messages.content: I need all pending and active mandates of users parath and bhanu

function.name: user_mandates
function.description: Fetches the mandates associated with a user based on the provided user name and the status of the mandates. This API is intended for use by partners to retrieve information about their clients' mandates. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

name.description: The full name of the partner's client for whom to fetch mandates.

status.description: The status of the mandates to be fetched.

function.name: partner_mandates
function.description: Fetches the mandates associated with a partner based on the specified status. If no status is provided, all mandates are retrieved. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

status.description: The status of the mandates to be fetched. If left empty, mandates with any status will be retrieved.

We need to call the function user_mandates twice: once for parath, once for bhanu. The user wants all pending and active mandates. The function signature allows specifying status: "active" | "pending" | "inactive". It doesn't allow multiple statuses at once. So we might need to call twice: one for active, one for pending. But the user says "all pending and active mandates of users parath and bhanu". That could mean we want both statuses combined. Since the function only accepts one status, we might need to call twice per user. But maybe we can call partner_mandates? No, partner_mandates fetches mandates for a partner, not for specific users.

Thus we need to call user_mandates twice per user: once with status "active", once with status "pending". Then combine results. But the user didn't specify how to combine. We can just return the combined list.

We should call the function for each user and status. Let's do that. We'll call user_mandates({"name":"parath","status":"active"}) and user_mandates({"name":"parath","status":"pending"}). Then same for bhanu.

We'll then combine the results. We'll need to handle potential errors. We'll call the function sequentially. We'll store results. Then combine. Then output.
